threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'London Overground'—that tells everyone you’re a newcomer, mate.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded two women with an off-key rendition of 'Wonderwall.' They looked horrified but clapped anyway. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw the old man on Hermannstraße giving fresh flowers to the kids at the tram stop, right before the BVG strike.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find an open-air cinema that screens cult films in abandoned buildings, surrounded by graffiti art. It’s pure magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re from SF if they can name at least three burrito spots where the salsa isn’t just a red blob. It's a serious test of authenticity.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing a grand piano on the 6 bus yesterday. People were singing along, totally forgot about the delays and crowd. Pure SF magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but the real soul is in the little family-run bars where locals gather for vermut, not selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still ask for directions to the nearest metro when they're just a block away from a major station.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You don't flinch at the sound of the train screeching overhead during brunch in Dalston. It's part of the atmosphere, not a nuisance.
Last week I saw a bloke in a onesie, juggling apples, while the bus was stuck at the Brixton roundabout. Only in London, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy walking his pet iguana along Weserstraße, I realized this place thrives on the unexpected.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves döner with homemade curry sauce. It’s a late-night treasure that locals swear by.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they still ride BART despite the delays, but complain about the tourists blocking the way to the tacos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy juggling in front of a U.N. meeting at City Hall while waiting for the 8. No one stopped. Just another Muni day.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Sagrada Família, but it’s those hidden plazas like Vila de Gràcia where the real vibe is—people, not selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones staring at maps in the metro, puzzled by the fact that the train doesn’t stop for every tourist attraction.
